highlights.text: al-baṣal (البصل) is simply "the onion"
"Massive, strong-scented, bound by its straps... of Qurdumānī and Turkish make, like the onion."
a single root whose core sense is the selling of a thing
Verb بِعْتُ الشَّيْءَ بَيْعًا ("I sold the thing")
Ibn Fāris cites the Prophetic saying "Let none of you sell over the sale of his brother," which the scholars glossed as "let none buy over his brother's purchase"
so whoever may sell a horse — our steed is not for sale
a single core notion: ugliness or foulness in a thing
al-fāḥisha (a gross or indecent act)
"I see death picking off the noble and selecting out the wealth of the tight-fisted miser."
a single sound root whose core meaning is pleasantness
"fruit," so named because it is found agreeable and delightful
light-hearted jesting or banter
a single sound root whose core idea is reaching the extreme limit of something — arriving at its very utmost
الغَرَق, drowning in water (submersion carried to its limit)
admiration and wonder at the beauty of a thing
aghraytuhu is explained through al-ghira' - the substance by which things are glued or stuck together (i.e. glue)
a single, unified meaning — plunging or descending down onto/into something that lies low or beneath a surface
al-ghawṣ (الغوص) is entering beneath the water — diving
a single-idea root: "intense thirst."
al-hīm — thirsty camels.
a single underlying sense: weakness
Al-hazl - "jesting," the opposite of al-jidd ("seriousness")
fixedness and clinging persistence
Lāzib is given as equivalent to lāzim
nor do they assume evil is "ḍarbata lāzib"
a single core sense: going away with a thing, that is, removal or erasure
The basic verb is mahawtu l-kitaba amhuhu mahwan, "I erased the writing,"
a single root meaning growth in something planted or cultivated
النَّبْت (nabt) is the familiar word for vegetation
أَنْبَتَتِ الْأَرْضُ means the land brought forth growth
the opposite of beauty — ugliness (al-qubḥ)
hādhā maqbūḥ wa qabīḥ — "this is ugly/disgraced" (near-synonymous forms)
indicates cutting a thing lengthwise
qadadtu al-shayʾa qaddan (imperfect aquddu) means "I cut the thing lengthwise"
The proverb says: "what brings your qadd up to your adīm (hide)?"
Putting something on and slipping into it
Leaping and movement
From this comes قميص (qamīṣ), a person's shirt or tunic
al-qirṭās is the physical writing surface itself: what a text is written upon (paper, parchment, or a scroll)
the plural of qirṭās, i.e., separate sheets or scrolls
holding/preserving something
a preserver of every thing
al-qūt, one's sustenance (what keeps the last breath of life going)
holding back from someone who bore him rancor
turning a thing on its head, returning its beginning to its end — i.e., reversal
glossed as: God returned them to their disbelief [because of what they had done]
the Prophet, brought stones for ritual cleansing, found a piece of dung among them, threw it away, and said "it is riks"
slackness or sagging in something
to make a thing look attractive to someone
white garments whose colour is brightened by rain pouring from "the sagging-bellied cloud" (al-ḥamal al-aswal)
driving something along
to drive (e.g. animals forward)
the walker is propelled along on it
Ibn Fāris cites Ruʾba: "lean of belly from running, long-backed, [firm] in the shank."
indulgence — a choice or special thing given to someone as a favour
A رَجُل مُتْرَف (mutraf) is a man who is indulged and kept in ease and comfort
one core idea: gathering together and taking refuge
**الْمَوْئِلُ** (al-mawʾil) — "a refuge" or "place of shelter,"
a single root idea: making something level and smooth, hence making it easy
waṭiʾtuhu bi-rijlī, aṭaʾuhu, "I trod on it with my foot"
coming to agreement on a matter
appears in the ḥadīth cited here: "Make your tread heavy upon Muḍar."
a single core idea: adjustment/balancing (taʿdīl) and straightness (istiqāma)
wazantu al-shayʾa waznan, "I weighed the thing."
a dying-down fire
khabat al-nāru takhbū means the fire's flame settled/subsided
"kullamā khabat zidnāhum saʿīran" ("every time it dies down, We increase them in blazing fire")
